# Amber CLI v2.0.18

Amber CLI 2.0.18 runs one Crystal compiler order everywhere and finds amber-lsp's LLVM next to that compiler. Generated applications pin the same Amber `v2.0.0-beta.16`, Grant `v0.28.2` and asset_pipeline `v0.40.1` commits as 2.0.17.

## What changed

- **One compiler order (#78).** Every command that runs Crystal (`amber watch`, `amber exec`, `amber database`, amber-lsp's lookup and the agent hook) runs the compiler named by the `CRYSTAL` environment variable when it is set, otherwise `crystal-alpha` when it is on `PATH`, otherwise `crystal`.
- **The agent hook reads `CRYSTAL`.** `CRYSTAL_ALPHA` and `acrystal` are no longer read; set `CRYSTAL` to choose a compiler. The generated hook is now version 7: run `amber setup:agent` in an existing app to refresh it.
- **amber-lsp runs only an llvm-config from the compiler's Homebrew prefix.** It looks for `llvm-config` inside the Homebrew prefix the chosen compiler is installed in (including the unversioned `llvm` keg), so the API index always builds against the LLVM that compiler was built with.
- **SQLite apps stay on the C library.** Generated SQLite apps move to Grant's own SQLite engine in a later release, after its durability soak finishes (#75).

## Upgrading

Install 2.0.18 and, in each app that uses the agent hook, run `amber setup:agent`. If you set `CRYSTAL_ALPHA` or relied on an `acrystal` command, set `CRYSTAL` to that compiler instead.

## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.22.3-incremental-4

Tracks upstream [Crystal 1.22.3](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.22.3). This is [1.22.3-incremental-3](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/releases/tag/v1.22.3-incremental-3) with one fix; the compiler and every other stdlib file are unchanged.

### Fixed: the standard library docs build again

- **`crystal docs src/docs_main.cr` succeeds** ([#80](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/80), "Stdlib docs load one Compress::Deflate backend"). `docs_main.cr` required `./compress/**`, which loaded both `compress/deflate/lib_z` and `compress/deflate/mica`; both define `Compress::Deflate::Reader`, so the build stopped with "this 'initialize' doesn't explicitly initialize instance variable '@inflater'". The docs now require `compress/deflate`, `gzip`, `zlib` and `zip`, whose entry files pick the backend with `flag?(:use_libz)`.
- **amber-lsp's stdlib lookup layer works with an empty cache.** `amber-lsp lookup` builds `src/docs_main.cr`, so with incremental-2 and -3 that layer was unavailable on every platform.
- The Agent Crystal Compatibility workflow now runs `make docs` after it builds the compiler.

The memory-ceiling work merged to `incremental-compilation` since incremental-3 (#56, #60–#79) is not in this release; it ships after its own release gates.

### Checked

At this tag's commit, `b9b8ba04e`, on macOS arm64 with an empty `CRYSTAL_CACHE_DIR`:

- The stdlib docs build exits 0, and the output documents `Dir.mkdir_p`, `Compress::Deflate::Reader`, `Compress::Zip::Reader` and `Digest::CRC32`.
- The docs also build with each of `-Duse_libz`, `-Duse_libyaml`, `-Duse_openssl`, `-Duse_pcre`, `-Duse_pcre2`, `-Duse_libiconv` and `-Dwithout_iconv`.
- On the same fix merged to `incremental-compilation` (`af6f425a2`), `make crystal` followed by `make docs` exits 0.

### Provenance

- Tag `v1.22.3-incremental-4`: annotated tag object `b9c2744ca1f4cbb7bec03e44422a50fdc0f8f9c4`, which peels to commit `b9b8ba04ec40b13e620ef1035ec4d51a24d4f287` on branch `release/1.22.3-incremental-4` (parent: incremental-3's `3923a40905a2c00983bfc61dbf2688e7a9bffd2f`).

Downloaded three times with the same hash each time; `git get-tar-commit-id` gives the commit above, and the unpacked archive is identical to `git archive` of the commit.
- Standard library identity (`src/` hashed the way the tap's lock does): sha256 `762a9135041852bd9d9a51ef52ab0bd4a3275af785e1b5c50b52c0f8c47d01ee` over 2041 files; the 22 directory aliases are unchanged.
- `src/SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is unchanged at `1794528000`, so `crystal --version` prints `Crystal 1.22.3 (2026-11-13)`.

Install via Homebrew:
```bash
brew install crimson-knight/agent-crystal/agent-crystal
```

Or build from source:
```bash
git clone --branch v1.22.3-incremental-4 https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal
cd crystal
make crystal release=1
```

# Amber CLI v2.0.17

Amber CLI 2.0.17 generates applications on Amber `v2.0.0-beta.16`, Grant `v0.28.2` and asset_pipeline `v0.40.1`: the Amber stack's Beryl adoption release. An `amber new` app links no OpenSSL, with no flag and no setting, with or without `--tls`, on SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL. TLS 1.3 is the only version spoken.

## What changed

- **New apps pin the Beryl release by commit**, and `amber new` checks each one's checksum in `shard.lock`:
  - Amber `261cf2d3b4a6f3292fefb8113e71e0fe6900fcee # v2.0.0-beta.16` (`sha256-v2:9f7aa2e4…`)
  - Grant `4ba859e673a85de91b5dd815556ee83be3cc13b2 # v0.28.2` (`sha256-v2:cd018dbf…`)
  - asset_pipeline `9a0447c0e10d645307e8532c7794b89491281210 # v0.40.1` (`sha256-v2:d34f0ec9…`)
  - for `-d mysql`, crimson-knight/crystal-mysql `ce9cbfab8ba76f5b6d25386140aca0a409b1d585` (0.18.1)
- **`amber new --tls` (#72)** serves HTTPS from Beryl TLS 1.3 with the same `server.ssl` settings.
- **`amber database` runs on Grant (#77).** Migrations, rollback, redo, status, version, create and drop run on `Grant::Tasks::Database`, with the same drivers the app uses: Grant's PostgreSQL driver and crystal-mysql on Beryl TLS 1.3, and Grant's SQLite driver on the system's libsqlite3. Micrate's `micrate_db_version` table is read and kept, so an app migrated by an earlier CLI continues from its last version, and every `db/migrations/*.sql` file with `-- +micrate Up` and `-- +micrate Down` sections runs unchanged. `drop` still refuses the production environment.
- **The `amber` binary links no OpenSSL.** micrate, will/crystal-pg, upstream crystal-mysql and crystal-sqlite3 are gone from the CLI, and `amber encrypt` runs on Beryl (the encrypted file format is unchanged; files sealed by earlier versions open).
- **Grant 0.28.2 compiles its own SQLite engine only when an app requires it**, so a SQLite app on the C library and the CLI itself link no PCRE2 on stock Crystal and build for Windows, and `amber database migrate` finds an app's migrations on Windows.
- **The CLI records its own git dependencies in `shard.lock` by git tree hash** (`git-tree:`), which every platform checks the same way; generated apps keep the `sha256-v2` checksums `amber new` writes for them.
- **SQLite apps stay on the C library in this release.** Generated SQLite apps move to Grant's own engine in 2.0.18, after its 72-hour durability soak (#75).

## Upgrading

Amber now speaks TLS through Beryl, its own TLS 1.3 written in Crystal. Your app links no OpenSSL, with no flag and no setting: HTTPS served by the app (`amber new --tls`), mail over STARTTLS or implicit TLS, and PostgreSQL and MySQL connections over TLS.

**To upgrade an existing app:** move the Amber, Grant and asset_pipeline pins in `shard.yml` to the commits Amber CLI 2.0.17 writes (and crimson-knight/crystal-mysql 0.18.1 for MySQL), run `minecart update amber grant asset_pipeline`, and rebuild. No code or `config/` change is needed.

**TLS 1.3 only.** Every peer must speak TLS 1.3: the browsers and clients of an app that serves HTTPS itself (every current browser, curl and Go do), your mail server, and your database (PostgreSQL 12 or later with `ssl_min_protocol_version = 'TLSv1.3'`; MySQL 8.0 or later). A peer that offers only TLS 1.2 is refused with an error that says so.

**Opt-out for one release:** build with `-Duse_openssl` to run the same settings through OpenSSL (still held to TLS 1.3). The flag goes away in the release after this one.

**Client certificates still need `-Duse_openssl`.** If your database login uses a client certificate (PostgreSQL `sslcert`/`sslkey`, MySQL `ssl-cert`/`ssl-key`), build with `-Duse_openssl` for this release; Beryl refuses them with an error that names the flag.

Private certificate authorities whose certificates have no authority key identifier now verify, as they do with Go and OpenSSL. `pg_dump` and `psql`, which Grant runs for structure dumps and loads, now verify the server with the same `sslmode` and `sslrootcert` as your app.

## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.22.3-incremental-3

Tracks upstream [Crystal 1.22.3](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.22.3) and includes everything in [1.22.3-incremental-2](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/releases/tag/v1.22.3-incremental-2) (#53, #50, #48, #52, #51).

### New: HTTP::Client and HTTP::WebSocket speak TLS through Beryl, with no OpenSSL

- **`require "http/client"` and `require "http/web_socket"` link no OpenSSL** ([#49](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/49), "HTTP::Client and WebSocket speak TLS through Beryl by default (-Duse_openssl opt-out)"). HTTPS goes through Beryl, vendored as `Crystal::Beryl` (Beryl 0.2.1, [amberframework/beryl@6afec738](https://github.com/amberframework/beryl/commit/6afec738)). A program that fetches `https://www.example.com` links no libssl or libcrypto and imports no `SSL_`, `EVP_` or `OPENSSL_` symbols.
- **TLS 1.3 only.** A server that offers only TLS 1.2 or older is refused.
- **`-Duse_openssl` opts back into OpenSSL for one release.** Client certificates need it.
- **On macOS the default trust store joins Beryl's pinned Mozilla roots to `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`** when `SSL_CERT_FILE` is unset. The macOS 27.2.1 file lacks the root that www.example.com chains to (SSL.com TLS ECC Root CA 2022); with the joined store the default client returns 200.
- **The `-Dwithout_openssl` compiler build is fixed.** The `require "./http/server/tls"` in `src/http.cr` is now guarded, so `make crystal` builds again.

### Build server and type inference (memory ceiling)

- **Run recorded macro programs eight at a time when checking a reuse** ([#54](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/54), "Build server: run recorded macro programs eight at a time when checking a reuse"). The report gains `program_runs` and `program_run_seconds`.
- **A typed proc literal keeps only the variables it can still use** ([#55](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/55), "Type inference: a typed proc literal keeps only the variables it can still use"). A long `routes` block of Amber route procs no longer holds a copy of every earlier variable per proc (about 1.3 GB on a 300-resource app).
- **The build server re-types a body that keeps its instance variable assignments** ([#57](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/57), "Build server: re-type a body that keeps its instance variable assignments"), so a new method called from a controller action no longer re-types the whole program.
- **The code generation child keeps the typed program as it is** ([#58](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/58), "Build server: the code generation child keeps the typed program as it is"), so the forked process shares its pages instead of copying them.
- **Unsafe `@[TypeOnce]` and `@[TypeBound]` uses are refused at compile time; `crystal tool strict --check` writes nothing** ([#59](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/59), "Refuse unsafe @[TypeOnce] and @[TypeBound] uses at compile time; make crystal tool strict --check write nothing"). The error names the method and the reason; `--unions` keeps alias unions whole.

### Checked

All at this tag's commit, `3923a4090`. Its tree differs from the tested #49 head (`fdc5dcb`) by #54, #55, #57, #58 and #59, so the #49 gates were run again at `3923a4090`. The comparison is base `8f5877265` (1.22.3-incremental-2). No suite has a failure that base does not have.

- **macOS 27.2.1 arm64 (M4 mini)**, compiler built with the pinned host compiler (agent-crystal 1.22.3-incremental-1) and LLVM 21.1.8:
  - `spec/std/http`: 716 examples, 0 failures with Beryl (the default); 712 examples, 0 failures with `-Duse_openssl`.
  - The compiler spec subset of alpha-ci.yml, `spec/compiler/semantic` included: 11684 examples, 0 failures, 0 errors, 9 pending (base: 11664, 0, 0, 9).
  - `HTTP::Client.get("https://www.example.com")` built with the default flags, run with `SSL_CERT_FILE` unset: 200. `otool -L` lists only libSystem (0 libssl/libcrypto), and `nm -u` shows 0 `SSL_`/`EVP_`/`OPENSSL_` imports. The `-Duse_openssl` control also returns 200 and links libssl and libcrypto.
- **Linux aarch64** (`crystallang/crystal@sha256:34ac3d5d…` build image):
  - `spec/std/http`: 716 / 0 with Beryl; 712 / 0 with `-Duse_openssl`.
  - Compiler subset: 11682 examples, 0 failures, 0 errors, 9 pending.
  - The example.com probe: 200, with 0 libssl/libcrypto in `ldd` and 0 imports.
- **Release compiler from `git archive` of this commit** (macOS arm64, `make crystal release=1`): builds in 188 s. With it, **amber_cli** (amberframework/amber_cli `release-2.0.17`, 16fb8dac) builds in the default multi-module mode with `CRYSTAL_DEFER_DEEP_CODEGEN` unset, and `amber --version` prints `Amber CLI v2.0.17`. The binary links only libgc and libSystem.
- **Earlier runs on the #49 branch** (Linux x86_64 under Rosetta, and std_spec on all three platforms): no failures beyond base. The five added PRs change only `src/compiler` and `spec/compiler`.
- **Homebrew bottles** for macOS arm64, Linux arm64 and Linux x86_64 are built, tested and poured from the tap by its Bottles workflow.

### Provenance

- Tag `v1.22.3-incremental-3`: annotated tag object `2957a530492c8c96bf826fbed49b55cf489ee476`, which peels to commit `3923a40905a2c00983bfc61dbf2688e7a9bffd2f`.

It was downloaded three times with the same hash each time, and `git get-tar-commit-id` gives the commit above. The unpacked archive is identical to `git archive` of the commit.

The 22 directory aliases are unchanged.
- `src/SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is unchanged at `1794528000`, so `crystal --version` prints `Crystal 1.22.3 (2026-11-13)`.


Grant builds on Windows again, and an app on the C SQLite library compiles
only the C library's path.

- **The engine is compiled in only when an app asks for it.**
  `require "grant/adapter/sqlite"` (the C library, the default) no longer
  compiles Grant's own engine; `require "grant/adapter/sqlite/grant_engine"`
  does, as before. On 0.27.0 and 0.28.0 the driver compiled the engine for
  every SQLite app, so an app on the C library reached PCRE2 through the
  engine's regexes on stock Crystal (13 `pcre2_` imports for a one-model app
  on Crystal 1.22.3; 0 now) and did not compile for Windows. Setting
  `Grant.settings.sqlite_engine = :grant` in a program that did not require
  the engine raises `ArgumentError`, naming the require, as `:libsqlite3`
  already did without the C library.
- **Windows.** The engine's operating-system files use POSIX locks, mmap(2)
  and localtime_r. On Windows they are left out: opening a database file
  through the engine raises `Grant::SQLiteEngine::UnsupportedPlatform`,
  naming the C library, and the engine's date functions take local time
  from Crystal's `Time`. Nothing changes on macOS or Linux. A CI job now
  type-checks Grant for x86_64-windows-msvc
  (`scripts/windows_type_check.cr`).

Minimum Crystal: 1.19.0

### Upgrading from 0.28.0

An app on the C SQLite library (`require "grant/adapter/sqlite"`) needs no
change. An app that runs on Grant's own engine requires
`grant/adapter/sqlite/grant_engine`, as the engine's documentation already
says; an app that set `sqlite_engine = :grant` without that require now gets
an `ArgumentError` naming it. Amber CLI 2.0.17 pins this release.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.16

Amber 2.0.0-beta.16 runs its TLS on Beryl, Amber's own TLS 1.3 written in
Crystal. An `amber new` app links no OpenSSL with no flag and no setting,
whether it serves HTTPS itself (`--tls`), sends mail over TLS, or talks to
PostgreSQL or MySQL over TLS. TLS 1.3 is the only version spoken.

This release ships together with Grant 0.28.0, asset_pipeline 0.40.1,
crimson-knight/crystal-mysql on Beryl, Beryl 0.2.1 and Amber CLI 2.0.17,
which pins all of them.

## HTTPS and mail on Beryl

`require "amber/tls"` (written by `amber new --tls`) now serves HTTPS from
Beryl: the PEM certificate chain in `server.ssl.cert_file` and the private
key in `server.ssl.key_file` (P-256, RSA or Ed25519), SNI, and ALPN
`http/1.1`. The settings are the same as in beta.15; nothing in `config/`
changes. A client whose handshake fails ends only its own connection.

The mailer's STARTTLS (`use_tls`) and, new, implicit TLS
(`use_implicit_tls`, port 465) verify the mail server's chain against the
Mozilla roots, or against `ca_certificates_file` (new), and its host name.

Measured on an M1 Max and an M4 Mac mini with a scaffolded `--tls` app under
32 keep-alive HTTPS connections: peak RSS 25.5 to 25.8 MiB with Beryl
against about 31 MiB with OpenSSL, and requests per second at or above the
OpenSSL build on both machines.

## TLS 1.3 only

A browser, client, mail server or database that cannot speak TLS 1.3 is
refused with an error that names the requirement. Every current browser,
curl, Go, PostgreSQL 12 and later (`ssl_min_protocol_version = 'TLSv1.3'`)
and MySQL 8.0 and later speak it.

## Databases on Beryl (Grant 0.28.0, crystal-mysql)

Grant's PostgreSQL driver and crimson-knight/crystal-mysql connect over Beryl
TLS 1.3: `sslmode` `require`, `verify-ca` and `verify-full` for PostgreSQL
(with SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS channel binding), and `ssl-mode` for MySQL. Without
`sslrootcert`, the chain is checked against the system roots (the file
`SSL_CERT_FILE` names, else the operating system's bundle). Private
certificate authorities whose certificates carry no authority key
identifier verify, as with Go and OpenSSL. `pg_dump` and `psql`, run by
Grant's structure dump and load, verify the server with the same settings.

## Opting out, for one release

Building with `-Duse_openssl` serves and connects through OpenSSL with the
same settings, held to TLS 1.3. Client certificates (PostgreSQL `sslcert`
and `sslkey`, MySQL `ssl-cert` and `ssl-key`) still need `-Duse_openssl`;

Grant 0.28.0 connects to PostgreSQL over Beryl TLS 1.3 and runs its tests
against MySQL through crimson-knight/crystal-mysql on Beryl, so an app on
Grant links no OpenSSL with no flag and no setting. It ships in the Amber
stack's Beryl-adoption release with Amber 2.0.0-beta.16 and Amber CLI
2.0.17, and carries Beryl 0.2.1 (certificates without an authority key
identifier, as private database CAs make them, now verify).

### Beryl 0.2.1

- The vendored Beryl moves from ed5f21e7 to 0.2.1: a leaf or intermediate
  without an authority key identifier is matched to its issuer by name and
  signature, as Go and OpenSSL do.
- Without `sslrootcert`, the PostgreSQL driver checks the server against the
  system roots; on macOS that is now /etc/ssl/cert.pem joined with Beryl's
  pinned Mozilla roots, since macOS 27.2.1's file lacks roots the keychain
  trusts (SSL.com TLS ECC Root CA 2022, AAA Certificate Services).
- The MySQL development dependency (crimson-knight/crystal-mysql) moves to
  0.18.1 (ce9cbfab), which pins the same Beryl 0.2.1.

### pg_dump and psql check the server as the app does

- `structure_dump` and `schema_load` pass the database URL's `sslmode`,
  `sslrootcert`, `sslcert` and `sslkey` to `pg_dump` and `psql` (as
  `PGSSLMODE`, `PGSSLROOTCERT`, `PGSSLCERT`, `PGSSLKEY`), with
  `PGSSLMINPROTOCOLVERSION=TLSv1.3`. With `verify-ca` or `verify-full` and
  no `sslrootcert` (or `sslrootcert=system`), libpq gets the bundle the
  driver reads: the file `SSL_CERT_FILE` names, else the operating system's.
  A URL without `sslmode` gets the driver's default (`disable` on this
  machine, `prefer` elsewhere), and these values replace the caller's own
  `PGSSL*` variables. Before, the tools connected with libpq's defaults
  and did not verify the server.

### PostgreSQL TLS runs on Beryl TLS 1.3; no OpenSSL by default

- The PostgreSQL driver connects over Beryl TLS 1.3, written in Crystal, so
  an app on the PostgreSQL adapter links neither libssl nor libcrypto with no
  flag and no setting. `sslmode` `require`, `verify-ca` and `verify-full`
  work as before; `verify-ca` checks the chain only and `verify-full` the
  chain and the host name. Without `sslrootcert` (or with
  `sslrootcert=system`) the chain is checked against the system roots: the
  file `SSL_CERT_FILE` names, else the operating system bundle.
- SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS binds to the server certificate (tls-server-end-point)
  through Beryl.
- **TLS 1.3 only.** A server that offers only TLS 1.2 is refused with an
  error that names the requirement (set `ssl_min_protocol_version =
  'TLSv1.3'`, PostgreSQL 12 or later). Tested on PostgreSQL 17.12 and 19.0.
- `-Duse_openssl` keeps the OpenSSL path for one release, for servers that
  stop at TLS 1.2 and for client certificates (`sslcert`, `sslkey`), which
  the Beryl path refuses with an error that names the flag.
  `-Dwithout_openssl` is no longer needed and changes nothing.
- The driver no longer requires `http` (it needed only `URI::Params`), which
  had pulled OpenSSL in through `HTTP::Client`.
- `amber db create` and `drop` keep the TLS parameters of the database URL
  (`sslmode`, `sslrootcert`, `ssl-mode`, `ssl-ca` and the rest) on their
  connection to the maintenance database.

## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.22.3-incremental-2

Tracks upstream [Crystal 1.22.3](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.22.3) and includes everything in 1.22.3-incremental-1.

### Fixed: multi-module builds that failed to link

- **Functions deferred under an uncalled `fun` body are now generated** ([#53](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/53)). From codegen depth 8 on, a new function is declared and queued. The `fun` bodies no Crystal code calls (asset_pipeline's `crystal_ui_*_callback_dispatch`, for example) were generated after the last flush of that queue, so the end of their call chains was declared and never defined. A normal (multi-module) build of amber_cli stopped at the link step with six undefined `Pointer(Hash::Entry(...))#[]` symbols on 1.22.3-incremental-1 and 1.21.0-incremental-10; `--single-module` linked. The queue is now flushed again after those bodies, and a function still waiting at the end of IR generation stops the compiler with its name instead of reaching the linker.

### New: a warning for a setter that writes to a copy of a struct

- **`pointer.value.x += 1`, `points[0].x = 1`, `make_point.x = 1` and the like now warn** ([#50](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/50)), because the setter runs on a temporary copy and the write is lost. The message names the expression, the field and the struct, and shows the fix (copy to a local, change it, write it back). It is an error in a strict file (`# crystal: strict`). Writes that do land (`ptr.value.x = 1`, a local, an instance variable, a getter on a class instance) stay silent.

### wasm32

- **`--mattr` works on wasm32** ([#48](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/48)). The target's own features were appended without a comma, so `--mattr=+simd128` dropped both SIMD and exception handling and crashed instruction selection (`Cannot select: catchret`). Feature lists are now joined correctly for every target (armhf's `+vfp2` default had the same defect).
- **The collector runs on its own on wasm32** (#48). The WASI libgc had no stack base, so its collection trigger read a 4.28 GB stack and no automatic collection ran until about 1.4 GB had been allocated. `GC.init` now sets the stack bottom from wasm-ld's `__stack_high`. In the showcase probe the GC heap after 164 MB of short-lived arrays went from 250,150,912 to 5,570,560 bytes (Chrome linear memory 249.6 MiB to 13.9 MiB). Programs that called `GC.collect` by hand as a workaround can drop it.
- **`@[Link(wasm_import_module: ...)]` is honored again** (#48): `host.host_note` no longer turns into `env.host_note`.
- **wasm32 programs that use `Regex` build with no warnings** ([#52](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/52)). On 32-bit targets `LibC::SizeT` is `UInt32`, and `Atomic#swap`, `#max`, `#min` and the unwinder passed it to the deprecated `Pointer.new(Int)` overload; they now widen to `UInt64` first. A new spec cross-compiles a program touching Regex, JSON, YAML, Log, fibers and more for wasm32-wasi with `--error-on-warnings`.
- **Programs start when the host reports zero arguments** (#52). `PROGRAM_NAME` is empty when argc is 0 or argv[0] is null, and `ARGV` is empty when argc is 0, on every target. Before, a browser WASI host that reports argc 0 made `_start` raise `Cannot create a string with a null pointer`; a native binary started with an empty argv crashed the same way.

### Link errors name the missing library

- **When the linker cannot find a C library the standard library links, the compiler says which flag needs it and how to install it** ([#51](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/51)), for example `-Duse_libyaml` and `brew install libyaml`, with the Mica alternative that needs no C library. A compiler running from a Homebrew keg prints the exact `brew install`; others print the Homebrew and Debian package names.

### Checked

All at this tag's commit, `8f5877265`, built as a release compiler from `git archive` of that commit with the pinned host compiler and LLVM 21.1.8 (macOS arm64, M1 Max):

- **`spec/compiler-cli`** with the infer-reuse, incremental, memory-budget, strict, C allocator, missing-library, library-path, module-spill, released-body, semantic-data-release and struct-copy specs: 176 examples, 0 failures, 0 errors, 1 pending (the zero-argument WASI host example, which needs the wasm32 libraries and Deno).
- **amber_cli** (amberframework/amber_cli `main`, 84486c4) in the default multi-module mode: builds and `amber --version` prints `Amber CLI v2.0.16` (it failed to link on 1.22.3-incremental-1).
- **amber50** (Amber V2 + Grant, 50 resources), clean build with `--threads 4`: links in 99.9 s at a 1.54 GB peak; the app answers `GET /`, lists and shows the form, takes the form POST with 302 and lists the new row.
- **`--incremental` self-build** (`--threads 8`): clean 28.9 s, one-method edit 14.6 s, the rebuilt compiler runs (1.22.3-incremental-1: 28.3 s and 14.6 s).
- **`spec/compiler/codegen`** at this commit: 1968 examples, 0 failures (the 2 known `special_vars_spec.cr:18` errors), 6 pending.
- Spec suites from the PRs: `spec/compiler/semantic` 3498 examples, 0 failures (#53); `spec/compiler-cli` with all four wasm32 examples 77 examples, 0 failures (#52).
- **Homebrew bottles** for macOS arm64, Linux arm64 and Linux x86_64 are built, tested and poured from the tap by its Bottles workflow.

### Provenance

- Tag `v1.22.3-incremental-2`, commit `8f5877265dcfe9035166a3782cf81aca38b09a7c`.
- GitHub source archive `https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/archive/refs/tags/v1.22.3-incremental-2.tar.gz` (the URL the Homebrew formula pins): sha256 `61fa886f25d2679abed92ce6117d6b0ef29f4aaa5652a72cf5a2bf53f3f151a3` (5,735,304 bytes; downloaded three times, same hash; `git get-tar-commit-id` gives the commit above).
- Standard library identity (`src/` as the formula installs it, hashed the way the tap's lock does): sha256 `9747750ec4f06517cedad8dda0f9d380f3ff84d7fda78714e583158e181a1984`, 1925 files (1923 on incremental-1), directory aliases unchanged.

Install via Homebrew:
```bash
brew install crimson-knight/agent-crystal/agent-crystal
```

Or build from source:
```bash
git clone --branch v1.22.3-incremental-2 https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal
cd crystal
make crystal release=1
```

Grant 0.27.0 ships its own SQLite engine, written in Crystal (`Grant::SQLiteEngine`), as an opt-in. An app that requires `grant/adapter/sqlite/grant_engine` in place of `grant/adapter/sqlite` runs every statement on the engine and links no C SQLite library, with no build flag. Its database files are ordinary SQLite files: they open in the `sqlite3` tool and pass `PRAGMA integrity_check`, and files the C library wrote open in Grant. Apps that keep `require "grant/adapter/sqlite"` are unchanged; `Grant.settings.sqlite_engine = :grant` moves them onto the engine.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.15

Amber 2.0.0-beta.15 makes TLS opt-in, so a default app on crystal-alpha links
no OpenSSL without a build flag, and compresses responses with Brotli when the
client asks for it.

## TLS is opt-in: `require "amber/tls"`

Amber no longer compiles its TLS listener into every app, and its own files
require `http/server` instead of `http`, so Amber brings in no
`HTTP::Client`. On crystal-alpha 1.22.3-incremental-1, whose `http/server`
leaves TLS out unless a program asks for it, an `amber new -d sqlite` app with
a Post scaffold links none of libssl, libcrypto, libz,
libiconv or PCRE2 without any build flag (`otool -L` shows none, and `nm -u`
shows no `SSL_`, `BIO_`, `ERR_`, `X509_` or `EVP_` import). It serves `GET /`,
accepts the scaffold's form `POST`, passes its 12 specs, and peaked at 18.2
MiB of RSS under load at the 8 MiB starting heap on an M4 Mac mini, against
20.0 MiB for the beta.14 app built by the same compiler.

An app that serves HTTPS itself (`server.ssl`) or sends mail over SMTP
STARTTLS (mailer `use_tls`) adds one line to `config/application.cr`, right
after `require "amber"`:

```crystal
require "amber/tls"
```

`amber new --tls` writes it. Without it, a server whose settings ask for TLS
stops at start, before it forks or binds, with
`Amber::Exceptions::TLSNotCompiledIn`, whose message names
`require "amber/tls"`. A `--tls` app served HTTPS with a self-signed
certificate (`curl -k` 200); it links OpenSSL, and peaked at 18.9 MiB over
plain HTTP and 32.2 MiB under 32 concurrent HTTPS connections.

On stock Crystal, `http/server` still requires `openssl`; `-Dwithout_openssl`
keeps its meaning there, and it cannot be combined with `require "amber/tls"`.

## Brotli content coding

`Amber::Pipe::Compression` offers Brotli, gzip and deflate and picks the one
the client accepts best, with `Accept-Encoding` q-values honored (RFC 9110,
section 12.5.3); on a tie Brotli comes first. Brotli comes from a pinned copy
of Mica's pure-Crystal encoder at quality 5, so an app links no libbrotli
(`Compression.new(brotli_quality: nil)` offers gzip and deflate only). A body
shorter than 1,024 bytes is sent without a content coding.
`Amber::Pipe::Static` serves a precompressed `file.br` as well as `file.gz`.
In a generated app, `GET /posts/new` with `Accept-Encoding: br` comes back
with `Content-Encoding: br`. A page answered from asset_pipeline's page cache,
such as the generated home page, is stored as gzip and identity only, unless
the app is built with `-Dasset_pipeline_brotli`.

## Vendored Mica and Beryl

- Mica moves to amberframework/mica `84812fd1` (component `compression`): the
  Brotli writer sizes its tables to a short body (amberframework/mica#34),
  Brotli decoding is at least as fast as libbrotlidec 1.2.1
  (amberframework/mica#35), and the Deflate and Zlib readers stop at the end
  of the stream (amberframework/mica#38). The encoder stays the Z6b port of
  libbrotlienc 1.2.1.
- Beryl moves to amberframework/beryl `b1df8cc1`: the hashes, HMAC, HKDF and
  AEADs Amber calls run with the processor's Data Independent Timing mode on
  (amberframework/beryl#9) and give the same bytes. The copy also carries the
  public-key code (F3b) and the x86-64 timing fix (amberframework/beryl#18),
  which Amber does not call.

Both are pinned by commit and per-file sha256.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.16 for new apps; it pins Amber `v2.0.0-beta.15`, Grant
`v0.26.0` and asset_pipeline `v0.40.0`, and `amber new --tls` makes an app
that serves HTTPS itself. For an existing app, pin the Amber and
asset_pipeline release commits in `shard.yml`, run
`minecart update amber asset_pipeline`, and, if the app serves HTTPS itself
or sends mail with `use_tls`, add `require "amber/tls"` after

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.14

Amber 2.0.0-beta.14 lets an app drop libz and OpenSSL, runs its cryptography
on Beryl at hardware speed, runs every regex on Mica, and applies
`logging.severity` from the environment file.

## An app can link no libz and no OpenSSL

Built with `-Dwithout_zlib -Dwithout_openssl`, an `amber new -d sqlite` app
with a scaffold, on Amber CLI 2.0.15, links none of PCRE2, libyaml, GMP,
libz, libssl or libcrypto (`otool -L` and `nm -u` both show none). It still
gzips its responses, accepts a form `POST`, and refuses a gzip request body
and a `charset=UTF-7` form with `415`. Under load at the 8 MiB starting heap
it peaked at 17.4 to 17.5 MiB of RSS on an M4 Mac mini, against 19.8 to
19.9 MiB for the default build of the same app.

The flags are opt-in. A default build still links libz and OpenSSL, because
Crystal's own `HTTP` and `OpenSSL` code requires them.

- `-Dwithout_zlib`: `Amber::Pipe::Compression` gzips and deflates with a
  pinned copy of Mica's DEFLATE, in Crystal, in every build. Grant's
  compressed columns and asset_pipeline's precompressed assets and stored
  pages use Mica too. `idle_compressors:` and the compressor pool are gone;
  a gzip response carries no modification time.
- `-Dwithout_openssl`: cookie signing and encryption, flash, encrypted files
  and COSE run on a pinned copy of Beryl. OpenSSL remains only for TLS, so
  the flag suits an app whose TLS ends at a proxy; in such a build
  `server.ssl` and mailer `use_tls` raise
  `Amber::Exceptions::TLSNotCompiledIn`.

## Cryptography on Beryl, at hardware speed

Encrypted cookies, encrypted sessions and `FileEncryptor` now write message
format version 2 (XChaCha20-Poly1305 under an HKDF-SHA256 key). Version 1
values are still read under the current and every previous secret and are
rewritten in version 2 on their next save. An app that rolls back to an
earlier beta after writing version 2 values signs its visitors out once.
`MessageVerifier` and `MessageEncryptor` accept `:sha256`, `:sha384`,
`:sha512` and `:sha1`; any other digest raises `ArgumentError` at
construction.

Beryl is pinned at amberframework/beryl `7d678c08`. Its hashes, HMAC and
AEADs run on the processor's SHA, AES, carry-less multiply and vector
instructions on Apple Silicon, Linux AArch64 and x86-64, and Beryl measures
every one at least as fast as OpenSSL 4.1.0 on an Apple M1 Max.

## Every regex runs on Mica

Every regex in Amber compiles on Mica, the default `Regex` engine of
crystal-alpha from 1.21.0-incremental-6, and CI checks each one.
`HTML.encode_entities` and `Amber::Markdown::HTMLEntities::Encoder` are
removed: no program that called them ever compiled.

## `logging.severity` sets the log level (#1461)

`logging.severity` (and `AMBER_LOGGING_SEVERITY`) was read but never
applied, so every app logged at `info`. An app now applies it once at boot:

```crystal
Amber.settings.logging.apply_severity_to_log
Amber::Server.start
```

Amber CLI 2.0.15 writes that line into `src/<app>.cr`. An app generated
earlier adds it after its last `require`.

## Performance guide

`docs/guides/performance.md` (#1471) gives the patterns, tools and settings
that make an Amber app fast and small from its first build, each with the
measurement it rests on.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.15 for new apps; it pins Amber `v2.0.0-beta.14`, Grant
`v0.26.0` and asset_pipeline `v0.39.0`. For an existing app, pin the three
release commits in `shard.yml`, run `minecart update amber grant
asset_pipeline`, add the `apply_severity_to_log` line, and run
`amber setup:agent`. Grant 0.26.0 writes encrypted attributes in format
version 2, which Grant 0.25.1 cannot read, so roll back only before new
values are written.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.13

Amber 2.0.0-beta.13 is a security release. It holds the `charset` a client
names on a form to the WHATWG Encoding Standard.

## Security: a form's `charset` is held to the WHATWG Encoding Standard (#1460)

Through beta.12 the `charset` a client declared on a URL-encoded form went
straight to iconv, so on Linux a request could open any converter glibc ships
by naming it. From beta.13 Amber accepts only the labels of the
[WHATWG Encoding Standard](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#names-and-labels),
in any letter case, and each label opens the one decoder Amber maps it to.

A form whose `charset` is anything else is answered
`415 Unsupported Media Type` before its body is read. That covers `UTF-7`,
`ISO-2022-CN-EXT`, an empty or oversized name, and the standard's
`replacement`, `x-user-defined`, `windows-1255` and `windows-1258` encodings
(glibc decodes the last two by holding back the final letter). The request
raises `Amber::Exceptions::UnsupportedCharset`, a `BadRequest`, and a schema
parse reports it as `unsupported_media_type`. A UTF-8 label parses the form
directly, with no converter. Multipart and JSON bodies never took an encoding
name from the request and behave as before.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Every app on beta.12 or earlier should upgrade. Use Amber CLI 2.0.13 for new
apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit in `shard.yml`, run
`minecart update amber`, and run `amber setup:agent`. Amber CLI 2.0.13 also
moves new apps to Grant `v0.25.0`, whose `BigDecimal` support is opt-in: an
app with `BigDecimal` columns adds `require "grant/big_decimal"` above
`require "grant"`. asset_pipeline stays at `v0.38.0`.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.12

Amber 2.0.0-beta.12 makes a default app smaller in memory and safer at the
door: it refuses compressed request bodies, stops keeping a session for every
visitor, and allocates less on every request.

## What changed

- **Compressed request bodies are refused (#1454).** A request with a
  compressed body is answered `415 Unsupported Media Type` before routing or
  any pipe reads it. Crystal before 1.21.1 inflates gzip and deflate request
  bodies with no size limit
  ([GHSA-jfq5-c3x6-w7jj](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/security/advisories/GHSA-jfq5-c3x6-w7jj)),
  so a 1 MiB body could become 1 GiB. The guard works on every compiler,
  crystal-alpha 1.21.0 included. An app that accepts compressed uploads sets
  `params.accepts_encoded_request_bodies: true` and bounds the body itself.
- **Sessions follow `session.store` (#1455).** See the behavior change below.
  `Amber::Pipe::Flash` writes the session only when there is a flash to keep
  or clear, so a visitor who never sees a flash gets no session. The memory
  session adapter keeps at most `session.max_memory_sessions` sessions
  (10,000 by default) and drops the one used longest ago. A `:web` route
  served to cookieless clients used to grow to 858 MiB in 90 s; it now stays
  under 15 MiB.
- **The logger allocates nothing when its lines are filtered (#1456).** At the
  default `info` level `Amber::Pipe::Logger` used to build every debug line,
  parse the params and create a session, about 11.8 KB per request, before
  `Log` dropped it.
- **`Amber::Pipe::Compression` (#1457).** It gzips or deflates responses with
  the same bytes as `HTTP::CompressHandler`, but its zlib streams come from
  `malloc` and are reused through a small pool, where `HTTP::CompressHandler`
  allocates about 270 KB from the collected heap for every compressed
  response. Amber CLI 2.0.12 apps use it through `CompressedResponsePipe`.
- **Asset tags are rendered once per manifest (#1458).** `stylesheet_link_tag`,
  `javascript_include_tag`, `image_tag`, `favicon_tag` and
  `javascript_importmap_tag` return stored HTML on later calls. A generated
  layout's three tags used to cost 6.9 KB per page.

## Behavior change: `signed_cookie` sessions live in the cookie

`store: signed_cookie` is the default in every generated app. Through beta.11
every store, `signed_cookie` included, kept sessions in the server's memory.
From beta.12 a `signed_cookie` or `encrypted_cookie` app keeps the session in
the visitor's cookie and nothing on the server. Session values travel with
every request and must fit in a 4,096-byte cookie (a larger session raises
`Amber::Exceptions::CookieOverflow`), the visitor can read (but not change) a
`signed_cookie` session, and `regenerate_session!` does nothing. An app that
needs server-side sessions sets `store: adapter` under `session:`, or
`AMBER_SESSION_STORE=adapter`.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.12 for new apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit
in `shard.yml`, keep Grant `v0.24.0` and asset_pipeline `v0.38.0`, run
`minecart update amber`, and run `amber setup:agent`. Check the `session:`
section of each `config/environments/*.yml` against the behavior change above.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.11

Amber 2.0.0-beta.11 carries the regex-free path from a JSON API to the whole
default app. An app made with `amber new -d sqlite`, with a Grant model and
asset_pipeline, links no PCRE2.

## What changed

- **No PCRE2 in a default app.** Grant 0.24.0 and asset_pipeline 0.38.0 keep
  `Regex` off their default require paths. The app Amber CLI 2.0.11 generates
  shows no `libpcre2` in `otool -L` or `ldd` and no `pcre2_` symbol in `nm`,
  before and after `amber generate scaffold` adds a Grant model. Amber CLI CI
  runs this check on macOS and Linux, and its control program that uses `Regex`
  must show PCRE2.
- **`respond_with` takes a `NamedTuple` (#1425, #1451).** The documented call now
  compiles. The tuple becomes `Hash(String, JSON::Any)` through its JSON form, so
  `Int32`, arrays and nested tuples work as values. `scripts/check_linkage.sh`
  answers one route this way.
- **`respond_with` takes any JSON-serializable `Hash` (#1451).**
  `Hash(String, String)`, `Hash(Symbol, Int32)` and the like used to fail to
  compile.
- **`Accept` q values count (#1451).** `respond_with` picks among the formats the
  response schema declares and honors `q`. `application/cbor;q=0` no longer
  answers CBOR, and a JSON-only schema answers JSON when JSON is acceptable.
- **A starting heap for the garbage collector (#1452).**
  `server.gc_initial_heap_mib` grows the collector's heap to that many MiB in
  every server process before it takes requests, and
  `AMBER_SERVER_GC_INITIAL_HEAP_MIB` overrides it. The default, 0, keeps the
  collector's own starting size, so existing apps see no change. Amber CLI 2.0.11
  writes 16 into every generated environment file.

## Keeping your app free of PCRE2

An app links PCRE2 again when it uses any of these, and it keeps working:

- `pattern:`, `filename_pattern:` or a custom `format:` on a schema field, and
  `validates_pattern` or a custom `validates_format`
- a `Regex` passed to `Pipe::CORS`, `Validator::Pattern` or `Validator::Format`
- Markdown, `strip_tags`, and the other `String` checks such as `email?` and `phone?`
- `request.cookies`; read `cookies` instead
- `require "grant/regex"` (for `validates_format_of`, the SQLite `REGEXP`
  operator and Regex entries in `filter_attributes`), and Grant's schema
  tooling, schema tenancy and sharding
- `Regex` in your own code

## Breaking changes

None in Amber. Grant 0.24.0 moves `validates_format_of` behind
`require "grant/regex"`; its release notes list the rest.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.11 for new apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit
in `shard.yml`, along with Grant `v0.24.0` and asset_pipeline `v0.38.0`, run
`minecart update amber grant asset_pipeline`, and run `amber setup:agent`. To
start the collector's heap at the size new apps use, set
`gc_initial_heap_mib: 16` under `server:` in each `config/environments/*.yml`.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.10

Amber 2.0.0-beta.10 takes the regex engine out of the request path. A JSON API
built on it links no PCRE2 on stock Crystal, and CI now fails if that changes.

## What changed

- **No PCRE2 in a JSON API.** On stock Crystal 1.22.2, an app with one GET and
  one POST shows no `libpcre2` in `otool -L` or `ldd` and no `pcre2_` symbol in
  `nm`, on macOS and on Linux. `scripts/check_linkage.sh` runs in CI, and its
  control program that uses `Regex` must show PCRE2.
- **Typed route rules (#1442).** Route parameter rules are types, and the router
  uses no regex engine.
- **Fixed patterns became plain code (#1443, #1444).** Amber's internal fixed
  patterns read strings directly, and no pattern uses lookaround.
- **Cookies, form keys, formats and backtraces (#1445).** The `Cookie` header,
  form keys, named schema formats, `String#url?`, backtrace frames and the
  exception page's code coloring use hand-written checks. Each check was compared
  with the pattern it replaced on generated input.
- **A crash removed.** `Validator::Format` with `FormatType::URL` raised
  `Regex::Error` on short crafted input. The new check takes time in proportion
  to the input.
- **One bad cookie no longer fails a request.** Amber leaves that pair out and
  keeps the others.

## Keeping your app free of PCRE2

An app links PCRE2 again when it uses any of these, and it keeps working:

- `pattern:`, `filename_pattern:` or a custom `format:` on a schema field, and
  `validates_pattern` or a custom `validates_format`
- a `Regex` passed to `Pipe::CORS`, `Validator::Pattern` or `Validator::Format`
- Markdown, `strip_tags`, and the other `String` checks such as `email?` and `phone?`
- `request.cookies`; read `cookies` instead
- Grant, whose query code uses `Regex` today
- `Regex` in your own code

## Breaking changes

- A route constraint is a rule, and a `Regex` no longer compiles. Replace
  `{"id" => /\d+/}` with `{"id" => :numeric}`. A rule judges the whole segment,
  so `{"cart" => /\d\d\d/}`, which matched `he110`, becomes
  `NUMERIC.with_length(3)`.
- A `Set-Cookie` header on a request is ignored. Specs that replayed response
  headers as a request must send `Cookie`.
- `Validator::Format::PATTERNS` is removed.
- Backtracer `app_dirs_pattern` is now the prefix list `list_of_app_directories`,
  and `modules_path_pattern` is now the prefix `modules_directory`.
- `Pipe::CORS` copies its origin list when it is built, and `cors.origins` holds
  strings and rule procs. `CORS.new` still accepts `CORS::OriginType`, and now
  also `Array(String)`.
- Phone numbers and the host of a `FormatType::URL` value accept ASCII digits only.
- The schema examples moved to `examples/schema`.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.10 for new apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit in
`shard.yml`, run `minecart update amber`, and run `amber setup:agent`.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.9

Amber 2.0.0-beta.9 adds what an application needs behind a proxy, adds a
security headers pipe, and ships its rules and guides with the framework, so a
language server and a coding assistant know them from the first edit.

## What changed

- **Trusted proxies (#1415).** `server.trusted_proxies` lists the proxies
  allowed to report a client's address and scheme. Amber resolves the client IP
  and decides HTTPS from those proxies only, reads one forwarding header family,
  and validates the setting before it starts serving.
- **UNIX socket listener (#1415).** An application can listen on a UNIX socket.
  The socket is created owner-and-group only, and a bind lock stops two
  processes from taking the same path.
- **`Amber::Pipe::SecurityHeaders` (#1422).** Sends `X-Content-Type-Options`,
  `X-Frame-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy` and `Referrer-Policy`, set through
  a typed `security_headers` section. Plug it into each browser, API and static
  pipeline. See the migration guide.
- **Rule pack for amber-lsp.** `.amber-lsp/packs/amber_v2.yml` checks for Grant
  models, the V2 security headers pipe, ECR views, the JSON perimeter, nil
  narrowing and output through `Log`. Each finding names the fix. Amber CLI 2.0.9
  or newer loads the pack with no setup and prints its guidance at the start of
  an assistant session.
- **API card for amber-lsp.** `amber-lsp lookup` now carries verified notes and
  compiler-error hints for Amber's controller, params, testing and job APIs.
  Public params and validator methods declare concrete return types.
- **Guides for coding assistants.** `minecart install` now copies every guide
  in `docs/guides/` into the application's `.claude/skills/`, with an index skill.

## Upgrade

New applications from Amber CLI 2.0.9 start on this release. For an existing one:

```yaml
dependencies:
  amber:
    github: amberframework/amber
    version: 2.0.0-beta.9
```

Then run `minecart update amber`. If the application runs behind a proxy, list
the proxy in `server.trusted_proxies`, because Amber reads forwarding headers from
listed proxies only. `HTTPS: on` is not read as a scheme signal.

An application that calls `Amber::Validators::Params` directly now sees declared
return types. Code that relied on the earlier inferred unions may need a change
at compile time.

## Release

The tag is `v2.0.0-beta.9`. The GitHub release for the tag states the tagged
commit hash, its tree hash, and the sha256 of the source tarball attached to
the release (`scripts/release_checksums.sh v2.0.0-beta.9` produces all three).
A file cannot carry its own tarball's hash, so they live in the release.
